citation: Lee, O., Quinn, H., & Valdés, G. (2013). Science and language for English language learners in relation to Next Generation Science Standards and with implications for Common Core State Standards for English language arts and mathematics. Educational Researcher, 42(4), 223–233. https://doi.org/10.3102/0013189X13480524
use: Conceptual discussion of language demands and opportunities within science and engineering practices, including implications for English learners.
boundary: An article discussing language in science practices is not a classroom intervention trial and does not establish how common or effective any particular strategy is.

citation: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine. (2018). English learners in STEM subjects: Transforming classrooms, schools, and lives. The National Academies Press. https://doi.org/10.17226/25182
use: Consensus synthesis of research and guidance on the varied linguistic resources, experiences and educational opportunities of English learners across STEM.
boundary: The term English learners names a context-specific population and should not be treated as synonymous with all multilingual students. The report synthesises multiple sources; it is not one independent primary intervention study.

citation: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine. (2019). Science and engineering for grades 6–12: Investigation and design at the center. The National Academies Press. https://doi.org/10.17226/25216
use: Consensus study report on organising Grades 6–12 science around investigation, evidence use and engineering design.
boundary: It addresses secondary science broadly and does not estimate a multilingual-specific teaching effect. The source is a consensus report, not an intervention trial.

citation: Page, M. J., McKenzie, J. E., Bossuyt, P. M., Boutron, I., Hoffmann, T. C., Mulrow, C. D., Shamseer, L., Tetzlaff, J. M., Akl, E. A., Brennan, S. E., Chou, R., Glanville, J., Grimshaw, J. M., Hróbjartsson, A., Lalu, M. M., Li, T., Loder, E. W., Mayo-Wilson, E., McDonald, S., ... Moher, D. (2021). The PRISMA 2020 statement: An updated guideline for reporting systematic reviews. BMJ, 372, n71. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.n71
use: PRISMA 2020 reporting guideline for transparent documentation of systematic-review questions, searches, selection, appraisal and synthesis.
boundary: A reporting guideline supplies methodological expectations, not domain evidence. No historical search or screening records exist for this four-publication instructional selection.
